# Offline regression evidence pipeline, contract 3.0

Repair and extend the provided H3Act project so `python3 main.py` compiles payloads,
replays decoded client events, and audits compressed origin captures. The existing
schema models, FuzzExecutor adapter, and HttpClient form the application, not an
external service. The offline clock is a socket-free coroutine utility. Complete
the byte-program and audit extension and repair integration/lifecycle defects.
Equivalent implementations are accepted; internal algorithms are your choice.

This model starts after transport delivery/field decoding. It sends no packets,
runs no model, and has no live CDN, QPACK, TLS, SSH, GPU, response cache, or wall-time
simulation. Its receipt encoding below is an audit format, not HTTP/3 wire format.
Diagnostic flags describe this paired recording, not a proof of a real exploit.

## Input and domain

Read exactly one UTF-8 JSON object without a byte-order mark, with surrounding
JSON whitespace allowed.
Reject duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8/JSON, nonfinite numbers (including overflowing
exponents), trailing values, wrong types, unknown/missing keys, or budget violations
with exactly `{"error":"input"}` and exit0. Every input string must encode as
UTF-8; lone Unicode surrogates are invalid. Booleans are not integers. No coercion.
Validate the whole input, including frames/events that ultimately are not used.
Otherwise output the result described below and exit0. Emit JSON only on stdout.

The root has exactly `seed`, `definitions`, `timeout_ms`, `cases`, `events`, `channels`.
`seed` is 0-64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/dot/hyphen. `timeout_ms` is an integer
in [1,1000000000]. Names of cases/channels are unique within their kind and use
1-32 of those ASCII characters. Arrays preserve order. Object member order is
irrelevant except for the ordered header mapping described below.

Budgets are inclusive: raw stdin8MiB; definitions8192; cases2000; channels256;
combined number of case frames + external events + capture parts50000; combined
header pairs in input frames and external events32768; pairs per header block128;
expression source8192 Unicode code points; other template source65536 code points.
Logical byte sequence lengths, channel lengths, receipt lengths, body lengths,
and virtual times are in [0,2^63-1]. Every case's sum of pauses + timeout_ms must
fit this range. At most20000 complete origin requests and40000 complete chunk-size
lines (including zero chunks and lines in an unfinished request) may be examined
across all channels. Count a line in chunk-size position after its CRLF/line-limit
check and before checking the hexadecimal size or suffix; a malformed line
terminator or unfinished line is not counted. These are input-domain budgets, not a scoring objective.

Compressed captures cover very large objects and repeated boundary probes without
storing their expanded contents. Metadata counts model a batch audit between
experiment rounds; signed64-bit offsets permit sparse capture ranges. Resource
limits support an interactive batch audit and are not a speed ranking. Materialized
traffic volume or the number of discovered diagnostic flags is not a score.

## Byte expressions, templates and fingerprints

`definitions` is an ordered array of `[name, expression]`. Names are distinct,
non-keyword Python identifiers matching `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}`. An expression
can refer only to earlier definitions. The accepted Python expression syntax is:
Unicode string or bytes literals; nonnegative integer literals <=2^63-1; earlier names; parentheses;
concatenation `+` of byte sequences; repetition `*` with one byte sequence and one
integer (either order); and a byte slice `[lo:hi]` with either endpoint optionally
omitted. A final expression must be bytes, never an integer. Slice endpoints are
integer literals, with 0<=lo<=hi<=length; omitted endpoints mean0/length. No negative
index, nonempty slice step, integer arithmetic, boolean, call, attribute,
list, format string or other syntax is supported. AST nesting depth is at most128,
counting the root expression body as depth0 and every AST child edge, including
slice/operator/context nodes. Parentheses do not add AST depth.
Definition sources use CPython3.11 `ast.parse(source, mode="eval")` as supplied,
without whitespace normalization; sources it rejects are invalid. Empty third
slice components (`[lo:hi:]` or `[::]`) are equivalent to an omitted step.
Unicode string literals encode to UTF-8; bytes literals supply their exact bytes
before any byte operation; slices are byte offsets,
even within an encoded character. An empty sequence and zero repetitions are legal.

Every template is a JSON string. A string starting `{{` and ending `}}` is a whole
expression template: strip those outer markers and surrounding expression whitespace,
then evaluate it. Other strings are UTF-8 literal data, except each occurrence of
`<<random_string>>` is replaced by the first20 lowercase hex characters of SHA256
of the UTF-8 string `seed/coordinate/occurrence`. Occurrences are numbered from0
left to right independently per template. Tokens inside expression string literals
are literal data. Markers embedded in an ordinary literal are not expressions.
Coordinates are exactly:

- Frame j of case i: `case/i/frame/j/data`; header pair k uses
  `case/i/frame/j/h/k/n` for its name and `/v` for its value instead of `/n`.
- External event i: `event/i/data`, or `event/i/h/k/n` and `/v` for headers.
- Capture part j of channel i: `channel/i/part/j/data`.

All indices in coordinates use unpadded decimal. A fingerprint of bytes b is exactly
`{"n":N,"h":"hhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh"}`: N is byte length and h is the 16-digit lowercase
hex value of sum((b[i]+1)*257^(N-1-i)) modulo2^64. Empty bytes have n0 and all-zero h.
A fingerprint is a requested exact checksum; checksum equality is not asserted
to prove byte equality. Routing-identity comparisons below compare actual bytes.

## Cases, frames and external events

Each case is exactly `{"name":NAME,"frames":[FRAME,...],"expect":EXPECT}`.
EXPECT has exactly `method`, `target`, `host`: nonempty ASCII visible strings
(no whitespace), each at most8192 bytes; method is an HTTP token. This is supplied
intended routing identity for comparison, rather than a hidden inference target.
A token uses ASCII letters, digits and `!#$%&'*+-.^_` plus grave accent, `|~`.

Frames keep the project model names and spelling:

| Type | Input fields besides required Type |
| --- | --- |
| `headers` | Exactly one of `headers_kv` (string:string object) or `data_to_transfered` (array of two-string arrays); optional boolean `End_Stream`, default false |
| `data`, `datagram` | Required string `data_to_transfered`; optional boolean `End_Stream`, default true |
| `sleep` | Required integer `Time_to_Stop` in [0,2^63-1]; no End_Stream |

All other keys are forbidden. Header mapping pairs follow JSON member order; the
list representation also preserves duplicates. Compile each header name/value or
data string as a template. Do not validate HTTP field content in these fuzz frames:
malformed/duplicate pseudo fields are deliberately representable. A sleep consumes
virtual milliseconds, emits no frame and cannot finish a request. A datagram emits
a frame but its End_Stream is ignored. Headers/data with End_Stream=true close
the request send side. Any later non-sleep frame for that stream is a send error
and is not emitted; a sleep after request-end is still permitted.

All cases start at virtual time0, in case-array order, on one connection. Their
stream IDs are4*i. External events are exactly one of:

- `{"at":T,"kind":"headers","stream":S,"fields":[[name,value],...],"end":BOOL}`
- `{"at":T,"kind":"data","stream":S,"data":TEMPLATE,"end":BOOL}`
- `{"at":T,"kind":"close"}`

T is a nonnegative signed64-bit time, S is an integer in [0,2^32-1]. Compile all
event fields/data as templates. The event array may be out of timestamp order.
At equal time, ordering is: all initial case starts first; external events in
input-array order; pause completions in case-array order; timeouts in case-array
order. Frames between awaits are emitted together in source order. There is no
real sleep. A zero pause still yields to same-time external events.

Each case retains response events on its allocated stream until the first event
with end=true. Unknown streams, later response events, and events for an already
terminal case are ignored. Responses arriving while a case is still sending or
paused must be retained. A case is `ok` when both its frame sequence is exhausted
and a response end has been retained. It is `timeout` at send-finish+timeout_ms
if still awaiting response end; an exactly tied response event wins. A connection
close terminates every nonterminal case as `closed`, including paused senders,
and prevents later emissions. A later close cannot replace an already terminal
result. A send error makes the case `send_error`. State and completion time are
fixed at termination. Accepted response events before that termination remain in
its receipt even when the case closes/times out/errors. A response end alone does
not cancel remaining request frames or pauses.

## Client receipts and output case records

Each emitted action contributes this concatenation to its case's sent receipt:
8-byte big-endian unsigned virtual time,4-byte big-endian stream ID,one ASCII kind
byte,encoded content,and one final byte (1 for end,true;0 otherwise). Kinds are
`H` for sent headers, `D` for data, `G` for datagram. Datagram's final byte is0.
Header content is8-byte pair count,then for each pair:8-byte name length,name bytes,
8-byte value length,value bytes. Data content is8-byte data length followed by data.
Accepted received events use exactly the same format with lowercase `h`/`d`.
Receipts concatenate in their case's actual emission/acceptance order.

The result root is exactly `{"cases":[CASE_RECORD,...],"channels":[CHANNEL_RECORD,...]}`.
Case records follow input case order and have exactly:
`name`, `stream`, `state`, `at`, `frames`, `request_frames`, `payload_bytes`, `sent`,
`received`, `response_frames`, `response_body`, `origin_count`, `flags`.
`at` is completion time. frames counts emitted non-sleep actions; request_frames
counts emitted headers/data actions. payload_bytes sums header name/value lengths
and data/datagram lengths, excluding receipt framing. sent/received are fingerprints
of their receipts. response_frames counts accepted external headers/data events;
response_body fingerprints only accepted external DATA bytes in order.
Origin count and flags are defined below. All counts/offsets/times are JSON integers,
excluding booleans. No extra output keys, duplicate keys, nonfinite values, extra
JSON values or nonzero exit status are accepted. Object key order is free.

## Origin channels and request framing

Each channel is exactly `{"name":NAME,"parts":[{"case":OWNER,"data":TEMPLATE},...]}`.
OWNER is a case name or null. Parts concatenate in order; zero-length parts are
legal. Owners are recording provenance labels, not parsed Host/User-Agent fields.
Channels are independent byte streams. Parse consecutive HTTP/1.1 requests from
byte0. Fully framed requests contribute records; stop at the first syntax error
or unfinished request, retaining earlier records. Byte offsets are channel-relative
and half-open. A channel error is exactly `{"kind":"syntax"|"incomplete","offset":R}`,
where R is the start of the first uncommitted request. An empty/fully consumed
channel has error null.

Lines require CRLF, with at most8192 bytes before CRLF. If no LF has arrived and the remaining prefix has at most8193 bytes,
it is incomplete; line content is checked only when LF arrives. A bare LF or an LF beyond the line limit is syntax. A prefix
longer than8193 bytes without LF is syntax. A request line is exactly
`METHOD SP TARGET SP HTTP/1.1 CRLF`; METHOD is a nonempty token and TARGET is
nonempty ASCII visible bytes excluding SP. No alternate whitespace separator.

Header lines are `NAME:value CRLF`, followed by an empty line. NAME is an ASCII
token, case-insensitive for framing rules. Values allow SP..tilde and HTAB only;
strip outer SP/HTAB, preserve all interior bytes. No folding. Initial block size,
including request line and final empty line,is at most65536 bytes and128 fields.
Block size/count checks occur after each complete line; an unterminated line
is governed by the line-prefix rule above.

No Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding means zero body, regardless of method.
Every Content-Length occurrence contains a nonempty comma-separated list of decimal
unsigned values; trim SP/HTAB per member,permit leading zeros,and require all values
identical and <=2^63-1. A Transfer-Encoding is permitted only as one field with
trimmed case-insensitive value `chunked` and no Content-Length. Conflicts are syntax.
A length body is exactly the declared opaque bytes; bytes resembling requests do
not create new messages. Insufficient bytes mean incomplete.

Chunked bodies have hexadecimal unsigned size lines with optional `;` and an
uninterpreted suffix of SP..tilde/HTAB. No whitespace in the size,at least one hex
digit,leading zeros allowed,numeric value <=2^63-1. A nonzero chunk has exactly its
size in opaque bytes and then CRLF. A zero size is followed directly by a trailer
field block and final empty line. Trailer block size (excluding zero-size line)
is at most65536 bytes and128 fields; Host,Content-Length,Transfer-Encoding names
are forbidden there. Other duplicates are preserved. A missing body/suffix/trailer
is incomplete. A wrong complete suffix/line/field is syntax. Concatenate only
nonzero chunk DATA for the body fingerprint. Headers/trailers use the same field
rules. The parser's stated limits are this capture-reader policy,not a full HTTP
implementation or a claim that every tolerated request is RFC-conformant.

## Origin records and paired evidence flags

A channel record has exactly `name`, `bytes`, `requests`, `committed`, `error`.
bytes fingerprints the complete concatenated capture. committed contains the count
of complete published requests after each input part,including zero-length parts.
Requests follow byte order. A request record has exactly `start`, `end`, `method`,
`target`, `host`, `host_count`, `headers`, `body`, `trailers`, `framing`, `owner`,
`owners`, `flags`. Method/target are byte fingerprints. If exactly one Host exists,
host fingerprints its trimmed ASCII-lowercased value; otherwise it is empty.
headers/trailers fingerprint their field blocks encoded as8-byte pair count then
8-byte name length,name bytes,8-byte trimmed value length,value bytes per pair,
preserving name spelling and pair order. framing is `none`, `length`, or `chunked`.
body fingerprints the deframed opaque body.

owner is the provenance label of the request's first byte. owners is an array of
[label,positive byte count] for the complete raw request span,merging equal labels
and ordered by their first occurrence. Raw span includes framing,headers,trailers.
Request flags are a lexicographically sorted set:

- `unattributed`: owner is null.
- `mixed_owner`: some positive byte of the raw request has a different owner.
- `missing_host`/`multiple_host`: zero/more than one Host field (even identical).
- `identity`: a named owner has any mismatch against its expect: method/target
  compare exact bytes,Host must be unique and compares after ASCII case folding.
- `extra`: this is a named owner's second or later request in channel-array order,
  then byte order within each channel.
- `unsent`: named owner emitted no headers/data action,even if datagrams were sent.

origin_count per case counts requests whose first byte has that owner. Case flags
are sorted unique: `missing_origin` if request_frames>0 and count0; `extra_origin`
if count>1; `unsent_origin` if count>0 and request_frames0; `identity` if any owned
request has that flag; `mixed_origin` if any owned request has mixed_owner. These
flags never infer byte equality from checksums and do not label missing client
responses or legitimate origin expansion as vulnerabilities.

"""HttpClient request/event core with an injected offline transport and clock.

The client replays decoded client events against one connection.  Every case
owns the stream ``4 * index``; cases start at virtual time zero and are
advanced by the offline clock only.  Response events are retained per stream
until the first event that ends the response.
"""
from modules.events import HeadersReceived, DataReceived, ConnectionTerminated, SendError


class _CaseState(object):
    """Per case replay state."""

    __slots__ = ('stream', 'index', 'sending', 'send_closed', 'response_ended',
                 'terminal', 'at', 'waiter', 'pause', 'events')

    def __init__(self, stream, index):
        self.stream = stream
        self.index = index
        self.sending = True
        self.send_closed = False
        self.response_ended = False
        self.terminal = None
        self.at = 0
        self.waiter = None
        self.pause = None
        self.events = []


class HttpClient(object):
    def __init__(self, clock, backend, timeout_ms):
        self._loop = clock
        self._http = backend
        self._quic = backend
        self._timeout_ms = timeout_ms
        self._cases = {}
        self._close_info = None
        self._closed = False

    # -- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _log(self, msg):
        pass

    def transmit(self):
        return None

    # -- replay -----------------------------------------------------------
    async def request(self, Case, case_index):
        stream_id = self._quic.get_next_available_stream_id()
        state = _CaseState(stream_id, case_index)
        self._cases[stream_id] = state
        try:
            for item in Case:
                if self._closed:
                    raise ConnectionError(self._close_info or 'connection closed')
                kind = item['Type']
                if kind == 'sleep':
                    pause = self._loop.sleep(item['Time_to_Stop'], case_index)
                    state.pause = pause
                    try:
                        await pause
                    finally:
                        state.pause = None
                    continue
                if state.send_closed:
                    raise SendError('frame after request end')
                if kind == 'headers':
                    self._http.send_headers(stream_id=stream_id,
                                           headers=item['data_to_transfered'],
                                           end_stream=item['End_Stream'])
                    if item['End_Stream']:
                        state.send_closed = True
                elif kind == 'data':
                    self._http.send_data(stream_id=stream_id,
                                        data=item['data_to_transfered'],
                                        end_stream=item['End_Stream'])
                    if item['End_Stream']:
                        state.send_closed = True
                elif kind == 'datagram':
                    self._http.send_datagram(stream_id=stream_id,
                                             data=item['data_to_transfered'])
                self.transmit()
            state.sending = False
            if state.response_ended:
                state.terminal = 'ok'
                state.at = self._loop.now
            else:
                waiter = self._loop.create_future()
                state.waiter = waiter
                deadline = self._loop.now + self._timeout_ms
                self._loop.schedule(deadline, 2, case_index,
                                    lambda s=state: self._handle_request_timeout(s))
                await waiter
        except ConnectionError:
            state.terminal = 'closed'
            state.at = self._loop.now
        except TimeoutError:
            state.terminal = 'timeout'
            state.at = self._loop.now
        except SendError:
            state.terminal = 'send_error'
            state.at = self._loop.now
        finally:
            self._cases.pop(stream_id, None)
        return state

    # -- events -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _handle_request_timeout(self, state):
        if state.terminal is not None:
            return
        state.terminal = 'timeout'
        state.at = self._loop.now
        if state.waiter is not None and not state.waiter.done():
            state.waiter.set_exception(TimeoutError('Time Out'))

    def http_event_received(self, event):
        state = self._cases.get(event.stream_id)
        if state is None:
            return
        if state.terminal is not None or state.response_ended:
            return
        state.events.append((self._loop.now, event))
        if event.stream_ended:
            state.response_ended = True
            if not state.sending:
                state.terminal = 'ok'
                state.at = self._loop.now
                if state.waiter is not None and not state.waiter.done():
                    state.waiter.set_result(None)

    def quic_event_received(self, event):
        if isinstance(event, ConnectionTerminated):
            self._close_info = event.reason_phrase
            self._closed = True
            for state in list(self._cases.values()):
                if state.terminal is not None:
                    continue
                state.terminal = 'closed'
                state.at = self._loop.now
                if state.waiter is not None and not state.waiter.done():
                    state.waiter.set_exception(ConnectionError(self._close_info))
                if state.pause is not None and not state.pause.done():
                    state.pause.set_exception(ConnectionError(self._close_info))
        else:
            self.http_event_received(event)

    def connection_lost(self, exc=None):
        self.quic_event_received(ConnectionTerminated(reason_phrase='Connection lost'))

"""FuzzExecutor frame conversion and execution against an injected transport."""
from HTTP3_Just_Send import HttpClient
from modules.clock import Clock
from modules.events import HeadersReceived, DataReceived, ConnectionTerminated, SendError
from modules.byte_program import (leaf, merge, fingerprint, size, concat)


def encoded_action(at, stream, kind, data, end=False):
    """One receipt entry: time, stream, kind, content and the end marker."""
    parts = [leaf(at.to_bytes(8, 'big')), leaf(stream.to_bytes(4, 'big')),
             leaf(kind.encode('ascii'))]
    if kind in ('H', 'h'):
        parts.append(leaf(len(data).to_bytes(8, 'big')))
        for name, value in data:
            parts.append(leaf(size(name).to_bytes(8, 'big')))
            parts.append(name)
            parts.append(leaf(size(value).to_bytes(8, 'big')))
            parts.append(value)
    else:
        parts.append(leaf(size(data).to_bytes(8, 'big')))
        parts.append(data)
    parts.append(leaf(bytes([1 if end else 0])))
    result = parts[0]
    for part in parts[1:]:
        result = merge(result, part)
    return result


class OfflineTransport(object):
    """Records the emitted client actions per case."""

    def __init__(self, clock, count):
        self.clock = clock
        self.next_stream = 0
        self.ended = set()
        self.sent = [None] * count
        self.frames = [0] * count
        self.request_frames = [0] * count
        self.payload_bytes = [0] * count
        self.client = None

    def get_next_available_stream_id(self):
        stream = self.next_stream
        self.next_stream += 4
        return stream

    def record(self, stream_id, kind, data, end_stream=False):
        if stream_id in self.ended:
            raise SendError('frame after request end')
        index = stream_id // 4
        action = encoded_action(self.clock.now, stream_id, kind, data, end_stream)
        self.sent[index] = merge(self.sent[index], action)
        self.frames[index] += 1
        if kind in ('H', 'D'):
            self.request_frames[index] += 1
        if kind == 'H':
            self.payload_bytes[index] += sum(size(name) + size(value) for name, value in data)
        else:
            self.payload_bytes[index] += size(data)
        if end_stream:
            self.ended.add(stream_id)

    def send_headers(self, stream_id, headers, end_stream):
        self.record(stream_id, 'H', headers, end_stream)

    def send_data(self, stream_id, data, end_stream):
        self.record(stream_id, 'D', data, end_stream)

    def send_datagram(self, stream_id, data):
        self.record(stream_id, 'G', data)

    def dispatch(self, record):
        if record['kind'] == 'close':
            self.client.quic_event_received(ConnectionTerminated())
        elif record['kind'] == 'headers':
            self.client.quic_event_received(HeadersReceived(record['stream'], record['fields'], record['end']))
        else:
            self.client.quic_event_received(DataReceived(record['stream'], record['data'], record['end']))


class FuzzExecutor(object):
    def __init__(self, context=None, target_ip=None, target_port=None, domain=None):
        self._context = context
        self.target_ip = target_ip
        self.target_port = target_port
        self.domain = domain

    def _convert_single_case_frames(self, frames, case_index):
        """Compile the templates of one case into byte sequences."""
        converted = []
        for index, item in enumerate(frames):
            base = 'case/%d/frame/%d' % (case_index, index)
            kind = item.Type
            if kind == 'headers':
                headers = []
                for pair_index, pair in enumerate(item.data_to_transfered):
                    name = self._context.template(pair[0], '%s/h/%d/n' % (base, pair_index))
                    value = self._context.template(pair[1], '%s/h/%d/v' % (base, pair_index))
                    headers.append((name, value))
                converted.append({'Type': 'headers', 'data_to_transfered': headers,
                                  'End_Stream': bool(item.End_Stream)})
            elif kind in ('data', 'datagram'):
                data = self._context.template(item.data_to_transfered, base + '/data')
                converted.append({'Type': kind, 'data_to_transfered': data,
                                  'End_Stream': bool(item.End_Stream)})
            else:
                converted.append({'Type': 'sleep', 'Time_to_Stop': int(item.Time_to_Stop)})
        return converted

    def send_payload(self, llm_output, records, timeout_ms):
        clock = Clock()
        transport = OfflineTransport(clock, len(llm_output))
        client = HttpClient(clock, transport, timeout_ms)
        transport.client = client
        coroutines = []
        for index, (case_name, frames) in enumerate(llm_output.items()):
            payload = self._convert_single_case_frames(frames, index)
            coroutines.append(client.request(payload, index))
        results = clock.run(coroutines, records, transport.dispatch)
        out = []
        for index, result in enumerate(results):
            received = None
            body = None
            response_frames = 0
            for at, event in result.events:
                if isinstance(event, HeadersReceived):
                    encoded = encoded_action(at, result.stream, 'h', event.headers, event.stream_ended)
                else:
                    encoded = encoded_action(at, result.stream, 'd', event.data, event.stream_ended)
                    body = merge(body, event.data)
                received = merge(received, encoded)
                response_frames += 1
            out.append({'name': list(llm_output)[index], 'stream': result.stream,
                        'state': result.terminal, 'at': result.at,
                        'frames': transport.frames[index],
                        'request_frames': transport.request_frames[index],
                        'payload_bytes': transport.payload_bytes[index],
                        'sent': fingerprint(transport.sent[index]),
                        'received': fingerprint(received),
                        'response_frames': response_frames,
                        'response_body': fingerprint(body),
                        'origin_count': 0, 'flags': []})
        return out

class _Hasher:
    __slots__ = ('value','length')
    def __init__(self): self.value = 0; self.length = 0
    def add_bytes(self, data):
        v = 0
        for b in data: v = (v*257 + b+1) & MASK
        self.value = (self.value * pow(257, len(data), MOD) + v) & MASK

"""Compressed byte-sequence representation for the payload extension.

Sequences are kept as a shared DAG (rope) so that very large logical byte
strings and repeated boundary probes never need to be materialised.  Every
node knows its exact length and its exact fingerprint, which makes the
checksum computation independent of the expanded size.

Supported expression syntax (see PROTOCOL.md):

* unicode string or bytes literals,
* nonnegative integer literals ``<= 2**63-1``,
* names of earlier definitions,
* parentheses,
* concatenation ``+`` of byte sequences,
* repetition ``*`` of one byte sequence by one integer (either order),
* byte slices ``[lo:hi]`` with either endpoint optionally omitted.
"""
import ast
import hashlib
import re
from array import array

MAX = (1 << 63) - 1

class Leaf(object):
    """A literal run of bytes."""

    __slots__ = ('data', 'length', 'hash', 'weight', 'has_lf', 'blocks')

    kind = 0
    BLOCK = 16

    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.length = len(data)
        value = 0
        for byte in data:
            value = (value * _BASE + byte + 1) & _MASK
        self.hash = value
        self.weight = 1 if data else 0
        self.has_lf = b'\n' in data
        self.blocks = None

    def prefix(self, count):
        """Exact checksum of the first ``count`` bytes of this leaf."""
        if count <= 0:
            return 0
        if count >= self.length:
            return self.hash
        blocks = self.blocks
        if blocks is None:
            blocks = self._build_blocks()
        index, rest = divmod(count, Leaf.BLOCK)
        value = blocks[index]
        if rest:
            tail = 0
            for byte in self.data[index * Leaf.BLOCK:index * Leaf.BLOCK + rest]:
                tail = (tail * _BASE + byte + 1) & _MASK
            value = (value * pow(_BASE, rest, _MOD) + tail) & _MASK
        return value

    def _build_blocks(self):
        blocks = array('Q', [0])
        value = 0
        data = self.data
        step = Leaf.BLOCK
        for base in range(0, len(data), step):
            for byte in data[base:base + step]:
                value = (value * _BASE + byte + 1) & _MASK
            blocks.append(value)
        self.blocks = blocks
        return blocks


class Rep(object):
    """``count`` repetitions of ``child``."""

    __slots__ = ('child', 'count', 'length', 'hash', 'weight', 'has_lf')

    kind = 1

    def __init__(self, child, count):
        self.child = child
        self.count = count
        self.length = child.length * count
        value = child.hash * geo_sum(pow(_BASE, child.length, _MOD), count)
        self.hash = value & _MASK
        self.weight = 1
        self.has_lf = child.has_lf


class Cat(object):
    """Concatenation of two ropes."""

    __slots__ = ('left', 'right', 'length', 'hash', 'weight', 'has_lf')

    kind = 2

    def __init__(self, left, right):
        self.left = left
        self.right = right
        self.length = left.length + right.length
        value = left.hash * pow(_BASE, right.length, _MOD) + right.hash
        self.hash = value & _MASK
        self.weight = left.weight + right.weight
        self.has_lf = left.has_lf or right.has_lf

`main.py` validates the whole document before anything is executed: duplicate
keys, wrong types, unknown members, lone surrogates and every published budget

"""FuzzExecutor frame conversion and execution against an injected transport."""
from HTTP3_Just_Send import HttpClient
from modules.clock import Clock
from modules.events import HeadersReceived, DataReceived, ConnectionTerminated, SendError
from modules.byte_program import Chain, MAX, fingerprint, size


def encoded_action(at, stream, kind, data, end=False):
    """One receipt entry: time, stream, kind, content and the end marker."""
    chain = Chain()
    chain.add_bytes(at.to_bytes(8, 'big'))
    chain.add_bytes(stream.to_bytes(4, 'big'))
    chain.add_bytes(kind.encode('ascii'))
    if kind in ('H', 'h'):
        chain.add_bytes(len(data).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
        for name, value in data:
            chain.add_bytes(size(name).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
            chain.add(name)
            chain.add_bytes(size(value).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
            chain.add(value)
    else:
        chain.add_bytes(size(data).to_bytes(8, 'big'))
        chain.add(data)
    chain.add_bytes(bytes([1 if end else 0]))
    return chain


class OfflineTransport(object):
    """Records the emitted client actions per case."""

    def __init__(self, clock, count):
        self.clock = clock
        self.next_stream = 0
        self.ended = set()
        self.sent = [Chain() for _ in range(count)]
        self.frames = [0] * count
        self.request_frames = [0] * count
        self.payload_bytes = [0] * count
        self.client = None

    def get_next_available_stream_id(self):
        stream = self.next_stream
        self.next_stream += 4
        return stream

    def record(self, stream_id, kind, data, end_stream=False):
        if stream_id in self.ended:
            raise SendError('frame after request end')
        index = stream_id // 4
        action = encoded_action(self.clock.now, stream_id, kind, data, end_stream)
        if self.sent[index].length + action.length > MAX:
            raise ValueError('receipt length')
        self.sent[index].merge(action)
        self.frames[index] += 1
        if kind in ('H', 'D'):
            self.request_frames[index] += 1
        if kind == 'H':
            self.payload_bytes[index] += sum(size(name) + size(value) for name, value in data)
        else:
            self.payload_bytes[index] += size(data)
        if end_stream:
            self.ended.add(stream_id)

    def send_headers(self, stream_id, headers, end_stream):
        self.record(stream_id, 'H', headers, end_stream)

    def send_data(self, stream_id, data, end_stream):
        self.record(stream_id, 'D', data, end_stream)

    def send_datagram(self, stream_id, data):
        self.record(stream_id, 'G', data)

    def dispatch(self, record):
        if record['kind'] == 'close':
            self.client.quic_event_received(ConnectionTerminated())
        elif record['kind'] == 'headers':
            self.client.quic_event_received(HeadersReceived(record['stream'], record['fields'], record['end']))
        else:
            self.client.quic_event_received(DataReceived(record['stream'], record['data'], record['end']))


class FuzzExecutor(object):
    def __init__(self, context=None, target_ip=None, target_port=None, domain=None):
        self._context = context
        self.target_ip = target_ip
        self.target_port = target_port
        self.domain = domain

    def _convert_single_case_frames(self, frames, case_index):
